The '''R4-series astromech droid''', also called the '''R4-series agromech droid''', was a highly successful attempt to capture a new market prospect&mdash;the [[Outer Rim Territories/Legends|Outer Rim]] urbanite who was more likely to have a souped-up [[Landspeeder/Legends|landspeeder]] parked in their garage than an [[T-65 X-wing starfighter/Legends|X-wing]]. Flushed with the success of their landmark [[R2-series astromech droid/Legends|R2]] launch, [[Industrial Automaton/Legends|Industrial Automaton]] rushed to capitalize on their new dominance of the [[Astromech droid/Legends|astromech droid]] market. Accordingly, the R4 was designed for life outside the pristine hangar bay. It was simpler, tougher, and cheaper than previous [[R3-series astromech droid/Legends|R3-series]] models.

==Description==
R4-series [[Astromech droid/Legends|astromechs]] shared the same body shell as previous [[R-series/Legends|R-series]] models, a barrel-shaped body with three [[Tread/Legends|treaded legs]]. The main difference was the [[Droid/Legends|droid's]] head, which was conical in shape.The R4 incorporated the advanced [[Intellex VI]] [[Computer/Legends|computer]] which was programmed with designs and specifications for commonly available [[Repulsorcraft/Legends|repulsorcraft]] and [[Realspace/Legends|space]] [[Transport/Legends|transports]]. Since it was never meant to be used in conjunction with military craft such as [[Starfighter/Legends|starfighters]], its [[RAM|active memory]] was only capable of holding coordinates for single [[Hyperspace/Legends|hyperspace]] jump.<ref name="EGTD" />

[[File:R3-R4_EGTD.jpg|thumb|250px|left|R3 and R4-series schematics]]
Standard equipment installed on the R6 included an [[Acoustic signaller/Legends|acoustic signaller]], [[Arc welder/Legends|arc welder]], [[Circular saw/Legends|circular saw]], a [[Holoprojector/Legends|holographic projector]]/[[Holorecorder/Legends|recorder]], retractable [[Manipulator arm/Legends|fine worker arm]], and retractable [[Grasper arm/Legends|heavy grasper arm]].<ref name="J7" /> In an effort to save money on the droid's production, equipment that had been standard on previous models, such as the [[Viewscreen/Legends|video display screen]] and the [[Fire extinguisher/Legends|fire extinguisher]], were removed.<ref name="EGTD" /> However, owners could fit that equipment easily into an R4 if they so desired.<ref name="AEG" />

Designed to be used in rugged work environments, the R4's chassis was able to shrug off minor nicks and dents. When given regular maintenance, the droid was able to outlast Industrial Automaton's estimates for operational lifespan, weather endurance, and recharge duration. Overall, the R4-series was cheaper, simpler, and tougher than their predecessors.<ref name="EGTD" />

==Role==
[[File:R4astromech.jpg|thumb|right|200px|[[R4-T8]]]]
Industrial Automaton marketed the R4-series to a different droid-buying market, that of an [[Outer Rim Territories/Legends|Outer Rim]] [[City/Legends|city]]-dweller who needed assistance with repairs and maintenance to their modified [[Landspeeder/Legends|landspeeders]]<ref name="EGTD" /> or household items like [[Holorecorder/Legends|holorecorders]].<ref name="AEG" /> Industrial Automaton had been faced with complaints about the cost of the R2-series and that the R3-series was perceived as "elitist" due to its exclusivity.<ref name="J7" />

Industrial Automaton believed that a droid capable of keeping equipment in good working order would be of interest to groups operating in the Outer Rim or off the regularly travelled [[Hyperspace route/Legends|hyperlanes]], especially if it was inexpensive. R4s had a loyal and helpful attitude, even more so than a typical R2. They were less independent however, and were unlikely to attempt repairs unless being instructed to do so. R4 owners came to see them as friends or pets, rarely [[Memory wipe/Legends|wiping their memories]] unless they changed owners, and that was not always guaranteed.<ref name="AEG" />  

==History==
The R4 was another successful release for Industrial Automaton with mass-market buyers praising the droid. Other groups beyond Industrial Automaton's target demographic found a use for the R4 as well.<ref name="EGTD" />

When an R4 unit that served the [[Jedi Order/Legends|Jedi Order]], [[R4-P17/Legends|R4-P17]], required a complete rebuild following an industrial accident on [[Gyndine/Legends|Gyndine]], it was refitted with a dome head similar to the R2-series rather than replacing the standard conical head. The rebuild was considered to be so successful that the Jedi began incorporating dome-headed R4 units into their [[Delta-7 Aethersprite-class light interceptor/Legends|Delta-7 Aethersprite]] and [[Eta-2 Actis-class interceptor/Legends|Eta-2]] starfighters.<ref name="NEGTD">''[[The New Essential Guide to Droids]]''</ref>

The [[Alliance to Restore the Republic/Legends|Alliance to Restore the Republic]], always looking for ways to stretch their resources, appreciated the droid's low cost and working knowledge of a wide array of general-purpose vehicles. During the [[Galactic Civil War/Legends|Galactic Civil War]], the conical-headed droids were common sights in Alliance bases and [[Hangar/Legends|hangars]].<ref name="EGTD" />

The [[Galactic Empire/Legends|Galactic Empire]] used a number of R4 droids aboard the [[DS-1 Orbital Battle Station/Legends|Death Star's]]. Fitted with nonstandard [[magnetic fault sensor]]s, they were deployed to find flaws within the [[Battle station/Legends|battle station's]] [[Magnetic field/Legends|atmospheric containment fields]].<ref name="EGTD" />
